newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus lodges complaint against TF1.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus lodges complaint against TF1.

text.p: Pay TV group Canal Plus said on Tuesday it had lodged a complaint against TF1 Publicite, the advertising arm of French TV channel TF1, alleging uncompetitive practices constituting an abuse of a dominant position.
It said it brought the complaint before the Conseil de la Concurrence, the French competition court.
At TF1 no one was immediately available to comment.
A Canal Plus spokeswoman said the pay TV group had requested that the practices which it complained about be dropped.
Financial daily newspaper Les Echos said on Tuesday that Canal Plus believed TF1 Publicite unarguably had a dominant market position.

Saying it was quoting from Canal Plus's submission to the court, Les Echos said TF1 Publicite had a market share of over 50 percent, while the market share of the other players was between 17 and 2.6 percent.
It also said there were barriers to entering the market.
Les Echos said TF1 Publicite's commercial conditions for 1996 contained several discounts based on the audience share of particular advertisers.
It said this had the effect of maintaining or increasing TF1 Publicite's market share despite a fall in the channel's audience.
Canal Plus' move is not the first legal battle between the two television groups. Last autumn TF1 unsuccessfully took Canal Plus to court, aiming to block its merger with Nethold.
